What this supplemental release includes

The December 2024 supplement to the GCMT offers an updated dataset on historical coal mine production worldwide. It covers 1,862 operational coal mines with a production capacity of below 1 Mtpa. The dataset includes historical production data from 2018 to 2023, with 2017 data included where available. It is divided into two tabs: "Historical Production (non-China)" and "Historical Production (China)". The "Historical Production (non-China)" tab contains data for 1,188 operating coal mines in 55 countries outside of China. The "Historical Production (China)" tab covers 674 operating coal mines in China.
How to use this supplemental release with the April 2024 GCMT

The full Global Coal Mine Tracker is updated annually. The last release was in April 2024, and the next release is scheduled for April 2025.

1. In both tabs, the GEM Location ID for each coal mine is included in Column A. Column "Status" shows the status of coal mines during the research period. Column "Capacity (Mtpa)" provides the annual production capacity of each coal mine. Column "Opening Year" indicates the year each coal mine began operations. The column "ROM or Saleable" specifies the type of production data available, whether Run-of-Mine (ROM) or saleable (see definitions below). When both types of data are available, we prioritize ROM data.
2. Please see the linked wiki pages in the Column "GEM Wiki Page" for all known information at the mine level.
Notes
1. For background, additional information, and references, see wiki pages for coal mines
2. For the GCMT methodology, see https://globalenergymonitor.org/projects/global-coal-mine-tracker/methodology/
3. For links to GEM reports using GCMT data, see "Reports & Briefings" at https://globalenergymonitor.org/projects/global-coal-mine-tracker/reports-briefings/
4. This database only includes coal mines with a capacity less than 1 Mtpa.
5. The Global Energy Monitor website provides a mapping tool for the last full GCMT release: https://globalenergymonitor.org/projects/global-coal-mine-tracker/tracker-map/

6. In both tabs, Column "Output Accuracy" indicates whether the production data is reported or estimated. Reported values come directly from referenced sources, while estimated values are derived using various assumptions.

7. In the "Historical Production (China)" tab, due to limited historical production data for most Chinese coal mines, approximately 80% of the data from 2018 to 2023 is estimated using the annual capacity utilization rate of the coal mining and washing industry (煤炭开采和洗选业产能利用率), as reported by the National Bureau of Statistics of China.
8. In the "Historical Production (non-China)" tab, Column B contains MSHA IDs for coal mines in the U.S.

9. In the "Historical Production (non-China)" tab, the "Coal Output (Annual, Mst)" columns contain annual production data for U.S. coal mines in million short tons (Mst), sourced from the Mine Safety and Health Administration (MSHA). This data has been converted to million tonnes (Mt) for consistency within the dataset.
10. All decimal data have been rounded to two or three decimal places.

11. Some coal mines have recorded production before their official opening year, often due to partial or test operations conducted before full-scale production, a common practice in China. Additionally, some coal mines may have been temporarily closed and later reopened or merged with other mines. The availability of opening year information depends on the sources we were able to identify.
